repo_title: AI in Detonation Spray and Detonation Spray Coating
author: William Sun with help from OpenAI

analysis.executive_summary: September 2026 showed clear acceleration of AI adoption around detonation spray and detonation spray coating, with the strongest momentum in process optimization, coating-performance prediction, and defect analysis. While several papers were broader welding studies, the directly relevant detonation-spray items highlighted two important trends: using AI/ML to model process–property relationships in spray deposition, and combining detonation-sprayed coatings with post-treatment or hierarchical design to push hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance higher. Notably, geometric deep learning for cold-spray thermo-mechanical prediction and segmentation of detonation/APS coating microstructures indicate that the field is moving from descriptive characterization toward data-driven control, faster screening, and automated microscopy analysis. Overall, the month suggests a transition from isolated coating experiments to digitally assisted coating development pipelines.
major_themes: AI/ML is increasingly used to predict spray-process outcomes from structured simulation and experimental data.
Post-processing such as UNSM is being studied together with detonation spraying to improve hardness, tribology, and durability.
Defect segmentation and microstructure analysis are becoming more automated through deep learning on SEM imagery.
Gradient and compositionally engineered detonation coatings are emerging as a route to better corrosion resistance.
Research is shifting toward linking process parameters directly to coating performance rather than reporting properties in isolation.
Hybrid workflows that combine simulation, data-driven modeling, and experimental validation are gaining traction.

notable_papers.title: Geometric and topological deep learning for predicting thermo-mechanical performance in cold spray deposition process modeling
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Not detonation spray specifically, but highly relevant methodologically: it demonstrates modern graph-based learning for spray deposition prediction, a template that can be transferred to detonation spray process optimization.

notable_papers.title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to detonation gun spraying; it isolates spray distance as a key control variable affecting porosity, adhesion, hardness, and corrosion behavior.

notable_papers.title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr3C2–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Shows how detonation-sprayed coatings can be further enhanced by surface modification, with detailed hardness and scratch-response data.

notable_papers.title: Study of the Corrosion Resistance of Cr3C2-NiCr-Based Gradient Detonation Coatings
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Important for detonation coating design because it examines gradient architecture and composition profiling as a corrosion-resistance strategy.

notable_papers.title: The Effect of Ultrasonic Surface Modification of Nanocrystals on the Surface, Microstructure, and Mechanical Properties of a WC-12Co Coating Deposited by Detonation Spraying
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the performance gains possible when detonation-sprayed coatings are paired with UNSM and quantitatively evaluated using statistical trends.

notable_papers.title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Provides a comparative baseline showing where detonation spraying sits among competing thermal spray routes for wear and corrosion resistance.

notable_papers.title: Ultrasonic Surface Modification of WC-Co-Cr Thermal Spray Coatings: Microstructure, Mechanical Properties and Performance
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Although broader than detonation spray, it includes DS coatings and demonstrates how post-processing can substantially increase microhardness and durability.

notable_papers.title: Defect Characterization and Segmentation in APS Thermal Barrier Coatings SEM Images Using BES-YOLO11
notable_papers.why_it_matters: Not detonation spray, but highly relevant for AI-enabled coating microstructure analysis; the same segmentation approach can support detonation-sprayed coating inspection.

field_progress: AI is becoming a practical tool for coating R&D rather than only an academic add-on, especially for predicting performance from process variables and microstructure features.
Detonation-sprayed coatings are being engineered in more sophisticated forms, including gradient structures and post-treated surfaces, to improve corrosion and wear resistance.
Quantitative microscopy is moving toward automated defect segmentation, which can reduce manual image analysis bottlenecks in spray-coating characterization.
The evidence base is expanding from single-property reporting to multi-property evaluation, including hardness, adhesion, scratch response, wear, and corrosion in the same study.
Comparative studies across APS, HVOF, HVAF, and detonation spraying continue to clarify where detonation spraying excels, especially in dense hard coatings.
Process parameter sensitivity remains central, with spray distance, gas ratio, and post-treatment load emerging as especially influential variables.
open_questions: Which machine-learning architectures best generalize across different detonation spray systems, powders, and substrates?
Can high-quality detonation coating performance be predicted reliably from limited experimental datasets, or are larger multimodal datasets required?
How should process parameters and post-treatments be jointly optimized to balance hardness, adhesion, roughness, and corrosion resistance?
What is the best way to integrate SEM-image segmentation with process data so that microstructure defects can be traced back to spray conditions?
How transferable are models developed for cold spray or APS to detonation spray coating diagnostics and optimization?
Can gradient detonation coatings be designed algorithmically for target environments rather than through trial-and-error powder selection?
analysis.outlook: The outlook for AI in detonation spray and detonation spray coating is positive and increasingly concrete. The most promising direction is a closed-loop workflow that combines process simulation, experimental coating synthesis, automated microstructure analysis, and predictive models for wear and corrosion performance. In the near term, AI is likely to have the largest impact in parameter optimization, defect detection, and data-efficient screening of coating compositions and post-treatments. As datasets grow and multimodal methods mature, detonation spray research should move toward faster, more reproducible coating design with better performance targeting and less reliance on manual iteration.
